verdict: Caution: lend selectively to Kanpur tanners with FTA-linked export orders and clean effluent compliance; avoid sub-scale job-work units with unhedged forex and thin buffers.
title: Kanpur leather tanning: a note to the credit manager
narrative:
## What the business physically is
A tannery buys raw hides and skins, soaks, lims, tans, dyes and finishes them, and sells crust or finished leather to shoe, bag and garment makers. **Cash is made in the drum, not in the showroom: yield per hide and chemical cost per square foot decide margin.** Kanpur's cluster sits in Jajmau and nearby areas, and the local units already make products to international specification [1]. The sector is fixed-capital and working-capital heavy, so debt funds both the drums and the hide inventory [11].

## Where value and cash sit now
**The single biggest cash risk is the wet-work shutdown: government regulation can close wet work for around 20-30 days, so units must hold 1-2 months of inventory to keep running [10].** That inventory is your real exposure, not the plant. Peer Super Tannery's Jun-2026 revenue was Rs 76 Cr, up 9.4% YoY, with net profit Rs 3 Cr, up 5.3% YoY [4] — modest growth, thin profit. Forex is a live leak: Super Tannery booked a Rs 0.45 crore fluctuation loss in FY24 against Rs 0.57 crore in FY23, with no formal hedging policy [8]. So when a proposal lands, check the hedging policy first; if the unhedged import portion is material, ask for the forward cover plan before sanction.

## What has changed
**The India-New Zealand FTA took effect 20 October 2026 and removed import duty of up to 10% on 181 products, including leather footwear, purses, belts, jackets and bags [1].** That is a genuine price-competitiveness gain for Kanpur exporters [1], and FIEO expects small and medium units to reach foreign buyers too [1]. The state is also promoting the cluster, with the leather fair inaugurated by minister Rakesh Sachan [3] and foreign buyers purchasing at the fair [2]. Set against this, India-wide exports are -3.0% Apr-to-date in USD [D] and bank credit is growing +11.9% YoY against output of +2.4% [D] — money is chasing slow trade. UP GST collections are +14.2% Apr-to-date versus India +6.1% [D], a local tailwind, but it is state-wide, not tannery-specific.

## Who to pursue, how to grow safely
**Pursue integrated tanners with own effluent treatment, a named New Zealand buyer or order, and a hedged import book; avoid pure job-work units and traders with no drum of their own.** Structure as a cash-flow loan against a drawing-power formula on stock and receivables, with a margin that survives a 20-30 day wet-work stop [10]. Take monthly stock-and-receivable statements, the forex exposure report, and the effluent consent status. Covenant a minimum hedging ratio on imports and a debt-service cover tested quarterly. Peer results are mixed — Bhartiya Intl net sales rose from Rs 2,800 m to Rs 3,728 m while Liberty Shoe fell from Rs 1,728 m to Rs 1,699 m [5] — so underwrite the buyer order, not the sector story.

## Early-warning signs
- **Inventory days crossing two months without matching orders** — the wet-work buffer has become dead stock [10]; freeze fresh limits and inspect godown.
- **Unhedged import payables rising while the rupee moves** — the FY24 loss pattern repeats [8]; demand forward cover or reduce the import line.
- **Buyer concentration in one New Zealand account** — FTA demand is new and unproven [1]; ask for the second buyer before enhancing.
- **Effluent consent lapse or pollution notice** — a shutdown follows directly [10]; stop disbursement until consent is renewed.
watch: Inventory days above two months with no matching order -> freeze fresh limits and inspect godown

Consent lapsed or notice received -> stop disbursement until renewed

Single-buyer concentration above half of export sales -> ask for a second buyer before any enhancement
